Welcome to the Bharti Airtel Limited and Bharti Hexacom Limited Q2 ended September 30, 2026 Earnings Webinar.

There is some seasonality of Q2, which comes in, as well as the pricing intervention that we took, where there is always a temporary impact on customer continuity and we will keep playing this out in terms of ARPU…
Capex for the quarter was about Rs.12,500 Crores, leading to a robust operating free cash flow, which is EBITDAaL minus capex, of over Rs.19,000 Crores.
willEndure: These initiatives are helping us mitigate inflationary pressures arising from ongoing geopolitical headwinds.
weaknesses: First, on the mobile revenue, we have grown slower than Airtel, 2.7% quarter-on-quarter growth versus Bharti’s 3.4%.

Now, if you look at 11.5% growth that we have had, obviously, you can see that there is an acceleration that is happening on the digital side, which is actually compensating for some of that managed decline on the core…

Welcome to the Bharti Airtel Limited and Bharti Hexacom Limited Q1 ended June 30, 2026, Earnings Webinar.
Post the management opening remarks, we will open up for an interactive

willDo: Post the management opening remarks, we will open up for an interactive
So, I understand that your annual capex is likely to be in the $4 billion ballpark.
Our operating free cash flow, which is EBITDAaL minus capex, was at over Rs.16,450 Crores.
weaknesses: Our consolidated net debt to EBITDAaL improved to 0.7% and India without passive infra is now lower than 1%.

While low entry level pricing helped attract customers, the outcomes were not consistent with the quality of customers franchise we wanted to build with a higher churn and weaker continuity in certain cohorts.
threats: These efforts have helped us in navigating this phase of global cost headwinds in the business.
